links.outcome: Inter-verifier agreement on evidence-conclusion coherence judgments across three LLM verifiers
links.effect: Fleiss' κ 0.087-0.223; disagreement 62.2%-74.3%; same rationale judged supported or unsupported depending on verifier; agreement with physician varied across verifiers (50 cases).
links.quote: Second, inter-verifier agreement on coherence is consistently low (Fleiss' κ 0.087-0.223; disagreement 62.2%-74.3%), so the same rationale can be judged supported or unsupported depending on the verifier.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-as-judge verifiers to automate evaluation of clinical reasoning coherence
Evaluating evidence-conclusion coherence of LLM rationales in addition to reference-based semantic metrics
Using unanimous-agreement tier of multiple LLM verifiers for selective automation of evaluation

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the reliability and disagreement of automated LLM-as-a-judge verification guardrails compared to physician adjudication for evaluating clinical reasoning.

primary.practice: LLM-as-a-judge automated verification vs human adjudication
